<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing a detailed, accurate system design diagram of AgenticSeek. We’ll identify each major “entity” (component or service), describe its purpose and technologies, and show how they interact. Use this as a blueprint to create a visual diagram (e.g., in Draw.io, Lucidchart, or your tool of choice).

1. Identify Project Type & Purpose  
   • AgenticSeek is a full-stack, local-first AI assistant platform.  
   • It combines a React single-page application (frontend), a Python-based backend/CLI core, multiple microservices (search, LLM routing, LLM server), and a browser-extension (CRX).  
   • Primary goal: run autonomous AI agents entirely on user hardware (no cloud dependency), with optional external API fallbacks.

2. Top-Level Components (Entities)  
   For each box in your diagram, include: name, responsibility, and technology stack. Color-code boxes by category (UI, backend, data store, external service).

   A. Frontend UI (React SPA)  
     – Directory: frontend/agentic-seek-front  
     – Purpose: renders web interface, captures user input, displays responses.  
     – Tech: React.js, CSS, Dockerfile.frontend, served at http://localhost:3000.  
     – Interaction: issues REST/WebSocket calls to Backend API.

   B. Backend Core (API + CLI)  
     – Files: api.py, cli.py, sources/  
     – Purpose: central orchestrator—receives requests, manages session, routes to agents, tools, or LLM.  
     – Tech: Python 3.10+, FastAPI or similar HTTP framework, Click or argparse for CLI.  
     – Key modules (detailed info below).

   C. LLM Router Service  
     – Directory: llm_router/  
     – Purpose: shuttle requests between Backend Core and one of the LLM providers (local or remote).  
     – Tech: Python script, config.json for routing rules, uses safetensors or curl libs.  
     – Exposes HTTP or CLI endpoints to Backend.

   D. LLM Server (Self-Hosted)  
     – Directory: llm_server/  
     – Purpose: wrap llama.cpp or Ollama into an HTTP API, enable remote LLM invocation.  
     – Tech: FastAPI app.py, handler classes for different runtimes (llamacpp, ollama), dockerized via Dockerfile.  
     – Used when provider_name=server in config.ini.

   E. SearxNG Search Engine  
     – Directory: searxng/ + docker-compose.yml  
     – Purpose: autonomous web-browsing/search aggregator providing search results to browser agents.  
     – Tech: SearxNG (Python), Redis for rate-limiting, custom limiter.toml, uwsgi, nginx.  
     – Communicates with Backend Core via SEARXNG_BASE_URL (HTTP).

   F. Redis  
     – Launched via docker-compose as dependency of SearxNG.  
     – Purpose: caching, rate-limiting for search.

   G. Browser Automation (Selenium Agents)  
     – Modules: sources/browser.py and sources/web_scripts/  
     – Purpose: drive headless browser (with stealth) to navigate pages, fill forms, extract content.  
     – Tech: undetected-selenium, JavaScript injection scripts, ChromeDriver via CRX extension.

   H. Agents & Tools (Business Logic)  
     – Directory: sources/agents/ & sources/tools/  
     – Purpose: encapsulate specialized behaviors:  
       • agents: planner, casual, coder, file, browser, mcp  
       • tools: interpreters (Python, Go, C, Bash, Java), search tools (flightSearch, searxSearch, webSearch), fileFinder, safety validator.  
     – Tech: Python classes, each agent picks the right tool set.

   I. CRX Browser Extension  
     – Directory: crx/nopecha.crx  
     – Purpose: integrate with browser automation; provides captcha bypass.  
     – Tech: Chrome extension.

   J. Configuration Store  
     – Files: .env, config.ini, .env.example  
     – Purpose: environment variables (service URLs, API keys, work_dir) and ini settings for providers, browser, speech.

   K. Docker Compose Orchestrator  
     – File: docker-compose.yml at root and searxng/docker-compose.yml  
     – Purpose: define and launch multi-container system (frontend, backend, searxng, redis, optionally llm_server).  
     – Tech: Docker, Docker Compose V2.

3. Relationships & Data Flow  
   Draw directional arrows:  
   1. User → (browser or CLI) → Frontend UI or CLI interface.  
   2. Frontend UI (HTTP) or CLI (stdin/stdout) → Backend Core (api.py / cli.py).  
   3. Backend Core → Router service (llm_router) → Local or remote LLM (via LLM Server or provider API).  
   4. Backend Core → Agent modules → Tool modules → optional Browser Automation (Selenium + CRX) or SearxNG (HTTP).  
   5. SearxNG ↔ Redis for caching/limiting.  
   6. LLM response and tool output → Backend Core → Frontend/UI or CLI → User.  
   7. Docker Compose manages container networking among these services.

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   • Microservices: LLM Router, LLM Server, SearxNG, Redis are separate containers.  
   • Layered: UI layer (frontend), orchestration layer (api.py/cli.py), domain layer (agents & tools), infrastructure (browser, search, LLM).  
   • Dependency Injection via config.ini and environment variables.  
   • Extensible Agent-Tool pattern: new agents or tools can be dropped into sources/agents or sources/tools.

5. Diagramming Guidelines  
   – Use clear rectangular boxes for each component; group related ones (e.g., agents/tools) in a dashed sub-region.  
   – Color code: UI (blue), Backend Core (green), Services (orange), Data stores (yellow), External (grey).  
   – Label all arrows with protocol (HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, CLI).  
   – Show environment/config as a side annotation feeding into each service.  
   – Indicate Docker Compose as the outer “platform” envelope.

6. Final Checklist for Your Diagram  
   – Boxes for: Frontend UI, CLI interface, Backend Core, LLM Router, LLM Server, SearxNG, Redis, Agents, Tools, Browser Automation, CRX.  
   – Arrows showing request/response flows.  
   – Labels on arrows (e.g., “POST /chat”, “queryLLM()”, “search()”).  
   – Color/shapes to distinguish internal vs. external/local vs. data store.  
   – A legend explaining colors and arrow styles.

By following these steps and detailing each entity as above, you’ll produce a comprehensive system design diagram that captures AgenticSeek’s architecture at a glance, yet with enough granularity to guide developers and architects alike.
